sources.label: Waverley Council - Marks Park coastal walk remediation

blocks.text: When a big storm rolls through, Bondi can change character in a matter of hours - and the short answer to "can I still go?" is usually no, not safely, and definitely not into the water. After heavy overnight rain in early April 2024, Waverley Council closed beaches and sections of the coastal walk, and a rock slip beneath Marks Park damaged part of the clifftop path between Bondi and Tamarama. Here's what actually happens on days like that - and, more usefully, how to check conditions yourself before you head down.
What a storm shuts down (and why)
Storms hit Bondi on three fronts at once, and each one triggers a different closure.

items: Dangerous surf. In a hazardous surf warning, lifeguards may fly the red flag (beach closed, no swimming) or narrow patrols to a single set of red-and-yellow flags. Ocean pools like Bronte and the Icebergs get pounded by waves washing over the edge, so they close too.

Unstable cliffs. Bondi's sandstone headlands soak up days of rain and let go without warning. The April 2024 rock slip below Marks Park is why Council fences off stretches of the coastal walk after heavy weather - a collapse can take the path with it.
Fallen trees and flooding. Parks and reserves close while crews clear fallen limbs, and low-lying paths and car parks can flood.

blocks.title: If the beach is closed, stay out of the water
blocks.text: A red flag means the beach is closed and swimming is prohibited - not "swim with care." Storm surf brings powerful rips that drag even strong swimmers out fast, plus debris and murky water. No swim is worth it.
How to check conditions before you go
This is the part I wish more visitors knew - you can save a wasted trip in five minutes from your phone. Here's my order of checks on a rough-weather morning:

items: Bureau of Meteorology - check for current severe weather, hazardous surf and rainfall warnings for the Sydney coast.
Waverley Council - the Beaches & coast and Parks & reserves pages, plus Council's social channels, carry the current closure notices for our beaches, ocean pools and the coastal walk.
NSW Beachwatch - pollution forecasts. After heavy rain, stormwater flushes into the ocean and Beachwatch typically advises against swimming for at least a day.
BeachSafe - Surf Life Saving's site shows patrol status and current hazards beach by beach.

blocks.text: After a big downpour, give the ocean a full day before you swim - even if the sun's back out and the waves look friendlier. Stormwater runoff pushes bacteria levels up, and Beachwatch's standard advice is to stay out for around 24 hours, longer after really heavy rain. The Bondi you want is the one two days after the storm, not the morning of.

items.label: Coastal walk
items.value: Sections fenced after heavy rain (rock-slip risk)

blocks.text: What to do instead on a storm day

Honestly, a wild-weather Bondi has its own appeal - as long as you keep your feet dry. I like watching the swell explode over the Icebergs wall from up on Notts Avenue, then ducking into a Hall Street café while it buckets down. Save the coastal walk and the swim for when Council reopens the paths and the flags are back up.

blocks.title: Check the coastal walk before you go
blocks.text: The section below Marks Park damaged by the April 2024 rock slip was fenced off for stabilisation work - check Waverley Council's current notices for its status before you go. Even between incidents, Council closes stretches after heavy rain as a precaution.

items.q: How do I know if Bondi Beach is closed today?
items.a: At the beach, a red flag means it's closed and swimming is prohibited. Before you leave home, check the Bureau of Meteorology for surf and weather warnings, and Waverley Council's Beaches & coast page and social channels for closure notices.

items.q: Is the Bondi to Bronte coastal walk open after a storm?
items.a: Not always. Waverley Council fences off sections after heavy rain because saturated sandstone cliffs can slip - that's what happened below Marks Park in April 2024. Check Council's Parks & reserves updates before you go, and never step around barricades.

items.q: Can I swim at Bondi straight after heavy rain?
items.a: It's best not to. Even once the surf eases, stormwater runoff raises pollution levels. NSW Beachwatch generally advises staying out of the water for about a day after rain - check its pollution forecast for the current recommendation.

items.q: Are the ocean pools open during a storm?
items.a: In dangerous surf the ocean pools close, because waves wash straight over the edge. Check the individual pool or Waverley Council for status rather than turning up on spec.

items.q: Where does official Bondi closure information come from?
items.a: Waverley Council manages our beaches, ocean pools, parks and the coastal walk, so their website and social channels are the authoritative source for closures. On the sand, the lifeguards, flags and posted signs always override anything you read online.

blocks.text: Storms pass, and Bondi bounces back fast. Give it a day or two, wait for the flags and the reopening notices, and you'll get the version of this place we all come for. Until then, respect every barricade and every red flag.
